title: Anomaly lane signal-folding and hypothesis playbook
content:
Summary:
This doc captures an experimental signal-folding workflow applied to the most recent onboarding eval (v2024-09) where we observed multiple low-frequency error slices that standard clustering missed. The goal: produce compact, actionable archetypes, map likely causal vectors (prompt formatting, context truncation, model variant mismatch, tokenization edgecases), and recommend short/medium/long mitigations we can ship in the next 6–12 weeks.

Evaluation snapshot:
- Model: open-variant-3B-quant (hosted candidate)
- Prompt set: 8k examples sampled from customer integrations + synthetic adversarial seeds (mix ratio 70:30)
- Metric signals: exact-match rate (EM), semantic-similarity (SS>=0.78), hallucination flag (classifier), latency, token consumption per call
- Failure signal threshold: EM drop > 15% relative to baseline OR hallucination rate > 6% on a slice

Why a new approach (signal-folding):
- Traditional clustering (kmeans, HDBSCAN on embedding space) grouped broad classes but diluted rare modes (1–3% slice) that still matter for customer SLAs.
- Signal-folding folds together orthogonal error indicators (semantic distance, tokenization anomalies, prefix overlap, response length patterns) into compact signatures, enabling identification of micro-slices that share remediation patterns.

Methodology (brief):
1) Feature construction: build a per-example vector combining: prompt-token-stats, normalized EM delta, hallucination score, top-3 token-prob entropy, KV-cache reuse heuristic, and truncated-context indicator.
2) Dimensionality reduction: UMAP (n_neighbors=12, min_dist=0.2) to preserve local neighborhoods for low-frequency signals.
3) Density modeling: use Gaussian Mixture on reduced space and post-hoc merge micro-components based on shared binary signals (e.g., truncated_context==true AND entropy>4).
4) Human-in-the-loop labeling: triage interface for rapid assignment of archetype names and preliminary root-cause tags.

Observed micro-slices (representative):
- Slice A "Leading-whitespace intent loss": prompts with leading newlines/spaces where the model drops the intent sentence and emits unrelated completions. (~2.8% of errors)
  - Representative prompt: "\n\nWrite a short description of the user's account activity:"
  - Hypothesis: tokenizer-leading-token misalignment + early-termination due to prefix-drop heuristic in runtime batching.

- Slice B "System-instruction bleed on multi-turn short context": short chat histories where a previous system instruction roughly matches user phrasing causing the model to over-weight system content. (~1.9%)
  - Rep: two-turn chat where system: "No PHI", user later asks for a health-related summary -> model either refuses incorrectly or returns redacted/blanked output.
  - Hypothesis: model conditioning and presence of a strict system token nearby; combined with aggressive context pruning, system token survives while user tokens get truncated.

- Slice C "Enumeration collapse on long lists": prompts asking for enumerations beyond the model's response-length budget; model repeats or collapses items and hallucinate fillers. (~3.5%)
  - Rep: "List 20 most common database sharding patterns and short pros/cons for each"
  - Hypothesis: token budget + attention pattern change in quantized kernels causing instability across long output spans.

Root-cause mapping (high level):
- Serving-level: runtime prefix-drop heuristics + batching-driven early cache eviction
- Prompt-level: leading/trailing whitespace, ambiguous system/user role mixing, implicit instruction density
- Model-level: quantization artifacts on distribution tails, degraded token-prob calibration for long-range generation
- Dataset/eval: sampled adversarial seeds reveal rare combinatorial cases not present in baseline training evals

Prioritized mitigations (by impact / ease):
Short-term (ship in 2 weeks):
- Pre-flight prompt sanitizer: strip leading whitespace-only prefixes, normalize repeated newlines, but keep single leading newline if explicit. Implement conservative rule: only remove if first non-whitespace char is alphanumeric and the first token is punctuation/empty. (Owner: Evan M.)
- Serving fallback: for prompts flagged with truncated_context==true and system_token_presence==true, route to a high-memory model-variant or enable soft-fallback that retains a larger prefix window for that request. (Owner: SRE/Serving)
- Heuristic response-length gating: cap long-enumeration answers and replace with "I can provide the first N items; reply 'more' to continue" template to avoid hallucination.

Medium-term (4–8 weeks):
- Prompt archetype rewrite library: curated rewrite rules per archetype (e.g., force explicit role labels, explicit list-length tokens, instructive separators). Deploy as opt-in per-customer rule set in console. (Owner: DevX)
- Calibration fine-tune on quantized kernels: small targeted fine-tune/LoRA on synthetic long-list data and leading-whitespace examples to rebalance tail token probs. Track EM/SS uplift. (Owner: Applied ML)
- KV-cache policy adjustment: change cache eviction to be LRU with prefix-stability bonus for last system and last user message. This reduces slice B. (Owner: Serving Runtime)

Long-term (quarter roadmap):
- Integration of signal-folding into continuous eval pipeline: auto-generate micro-slice alerts and suggested archetype patches.
- Model selection routing: train a slice-aware routing policy that picks a compatible model variant (quantized vs full, long-context vs standard) based on predicted slice membership.

Quick experiments to run (metrics to report):
- A/B test sanitizer on 10k incoming calls: measure EM delta, hallucination rate, median latency change, and false-positive rate of sanitizer (user-experience regressions).
- Run calibration fine-tune on dev split and measure improvement on held-out micro-slices + check regression on core seed set.
- Simulate serving fallback routing on replay logs to estimate cost delta and SLO impact.

Rollout plan and guardrails:
- Start with internal canary (10% traffic) for sanitizer rules + heuristic gating. Watch for regressions flagged by product smoke tests.
- Medium-term patches behind feature flag per-customer (DevX console toggle).
- Taxonomy updates: add a machine-readable archetype id for every micro-slice (e.g., AL-01, AL-02) and store mapping in the eval metadata for downstream dashboards.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is leading-whitespace primarily a tokenizer issue or is the runtime batching pipeline responsible? Need to repro with deterministic single-request runs (no batching) and compare.
- What is the cost delta of always routing system-token-heavy short contexts to larger-memory variants at 1% traffic scale? (Finance impact)
- Can we automatedly synthesize robust counterfactual prompts to expand training data for rare slices without producing distribution shift?

Action items (owners):
- Evan M: implement prompt sanitizer prototype + unit tests (due: 2024-09-30).
- Mariana G: set up replay-based fallback cost sim and run initial numbers (due: 2024-10-07).
- Asha P: create archetype id mappings and upload to Confluence; schedule triage session with product and SRE.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: we prefer quick, reversible mitigations over heavy model retrains where possible. Label any mitigation that has potential UX regressions in the PR description.
- Please review linked artifacts (Jira/GH/Confluence) and add any missing references.

References and logs:
- Perf traces: /logs/2024-09/anomaly-lane-rt-traces.zip (internal)
- Slack: #applied-ml thread "anomaly-lane-09" (search)
- Jira: AM-531 for dataset curation work

Unresolved items to capture after next run:
- Concrete thresholds for sanitizer FP rate (we set provisional 0.5% max).
- Definitive cost estimate for medium-term routing.

End.
